You are producing a component decomposition plan for the Frontend Development Lead of a Salesforce PWA Kit storefront (Zimmermann, luxury fashion). READ-ONLY: do not modify any repo file, do not commit, do not run `npm start`.

Repo: `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa`, branch `feature/SFCC-89_pdp-ui-static-product-information` @ `d526ad1`.

## The question, in the Lead's own words

"Based on the user story, the figma design, and what we have in the PR #55 for the footer, what are the atoms, molecules, organisms for these components? What is to be built from scratch? What is to be reused? What is for overriding? What is custom and not out-of-the-box?"

The team works **atom-first**: build atoms, compose into molecules, then organisms, then pages. Out-of-the-box (OOTB) Salesforce parts stay OOTB until their own ticket lands.

## Your three inputs — read ALL of them

**1. The user story (SFCC-89) and the Figma spec.** Both are already captured. Read:
- `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/4447dd18-bbe0-4a85-aae2-6e8935bf7947/scratchpad/req-jira.md` — the ticket, its six acceptance criteria, and the explicit in/out of scope lists
- `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/4447dd18-bbe0-4a85-aae2-6e8935bf7947/scratchpad/req-figma.md` — the measured design spec, including which text styles / colour tokens / spacing values map to existing repo tokens and which are gaps
- Also `conventions.md` and `code-state.md` in that same folder for what already exists

**2. The footer precedent — PR #55.** This is the reference implementation the Lead wants matched. It is on the local branch `feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui`. Do NOT check that branch out. Read it with git, e.g.:
- `git ls-tree -r --name-only feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui -- overrides/app/components overrides/app/theme/components`
- `git show feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui:<path>` for each interesting file
Work out the ACTUAL established pattern from the code: how are atoms/molecules/organisms laid out, how is styling done (theme recipe naming, registration), what naming conventions, what gets a story, what gets a test, how are shared/OOTB components consumed vs overridden. Note the `Zimm` prefix convention on theme recipes and WHY it exists (base SFCC recipes deep-merge via `extendTheme` if the key collides).

**3. What exists in the repo today.** Verify, do not assume:
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/` — what is actually in it on this branch
- `overrides/app/components/` — the full list
- `overrides/app/theme/components/` — which recipes exist and are registered in `index.ts`
- Which PDP-adjacent SFCC components have overrides and which do not (`image-gallery`, `swatch-group`, `display-price`, `product-view`, `quantity-picker`, `breadcrumb`, `product-tile`)
- What base SFCC ships that could be reused instead of built: check `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/` for anything relevant, and `app/components/shared/ui` (note: 103 relative re-exports, 212 base files import the barrel, 0 import deep paths — so overriding `shared/ui/<Name>` intercepts nothing)

## What to produce

**A decomposition table** covering every UI element in SFCC-89's scope (product name, price, description, style code, model copy, breadcrumb — plus the page-level layout/grid). For each row:

| Element | Tier (atom/molecule/organism/page) | Verdict | Why | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Where **Verdict** is exactly one of: **BUILD NEW** (custom Zimmermann, nothing to start from) · **REUSE AS-IS** (base SFCC or existing Zimmermann component, no change) · **OVERRIDE** (base SFCC module exists, we shadow it) · **THEME ONLY** (base component is fine, only needs a theme recipe) · **ALREADY BUILT** (exists on this branch already).

Tier assignment rule to apply: an **atom** renders no other project component; a **molecule** renders only atoms; an **organism** renders at least one molecule. An icon passed as a prop does not count. Slotted children do not count.

**Then answer each of the Lead's four questions explicitly, as its own short section:**
- What is to be built from scratch?
- What is to be reused?
- What is for overriding?
- What is custom vs what is out-of-the-box?

**Also include:**
- **A build order** consistent with atom-first — what to build in what sequence, and what blocks what.
- **What the current PR #57 got structurally wrong vs the footer precedent**, concretely. (Known: only one component sits under `ui-kits/`; two of the three new components have no theme recipe; the breadcrumb shadows a shared SFCC component consumed by the PLP.)
- **Token gaps** from the Figma spec that need a designer decision rather than an invented value.
- **Anything in SFCC-89's scope that has no Figma design** — flag it rather than guessing.

## Rules
- Cite `file:line` or `git show <branch>:<path>` for everything.
- Distinguish VERIFIED from inferred. If the footer branch does something you cannot explain, say so.
- Do not invent design values or component APIs.
- Note that `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/` has no rules file on `develop` — the layout convention is real but not citable. Say where you got it from.
- Do not propose touching Tier 1 files.

## Output
Write to `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/723a905e-37fe-4505-9a24-e817fe4260ab/scratchpad/q-decomposition.md` (create the directory if needed).

Then give a condensed version in your final report message, leading with the decomposition table.

Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

434 req-jira.md
# SFCC-89 — Requirements Picture

Research date: 2026-08-22 · Branch: `feature/SFCC-89_pdp-ui-static-product-information`
Method: Jira (issue + epic + links + subtasks + attachments), Confluence space SFCC, local `.docs/`,
plus a read-only cross-check against the code already on the branch.
**Nothing was modified. Read-only.**

---

## 1. One-paragraph summary

**SFCC-89 "PDP UI — Static Product Information"** (Story, High, 5 pts, **Sprint 3 (10–24 Aug 2026)**,
status **Code Review**, assignee **Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz**, reporter **Jasmijn Tsang**, due **2026-08-17**)
is the foundational PDP story: render the product fields that come straight off the SFCC product
record, with **no** dependency on Contentful, the colour/variation model, or inventory. Concretely
that is product name, single full price in the active storefront currency, product description,
optional "Model is…" copy (model height + size worn), style code, and a breadcrumb trail beneath the
product images reflecting the category path. The ticket's own description says it "is the most
foundational PDP story and should be built first." It is a **Level 2 page-level story** (parent epic
**SFCC-5 Product Detail Page (PDP)**), not a component build — which matters, because a **Level 1
component-epic story covering the same static fields now also exists (SFCC-737 `pdp/product-content`,
epic SFCC-2)**. Everything else on the PDP — badges, was/now price, swatches, size selector, CTAs,
gallery, accordions — is explicitly excluded and owned by named sibling tickets.

Fields **explicitly empty / not set**: `components` (none), `fixVersions` (none), `resolution` (none),
Story-point-estimate secondary field `customfield_10015` (null). Labels are set: `Custom`,
`DesignDependent`, `PRD-001`, `PRD-002`, `PRD-003`, `Squad-A`.

---

## 2. Acceptance criteria — verbatim, as a checklist

**Source: Jira field "Acceptance Criteria" (`customfield_10231`) on SFCC-89.** This field *is*
populated — it is not visible in the plain description, which is why it is easy to miss. Reproduced
verbatim below (original wiki markup flattened; wording unchanged).

> *Mandatory inputs for a Product to show on the website:*

**Product name**
- [ ] Given a shopper lands on a PDP, when the page loads, then the product name is displayed prominently at the top of the product information panel, sourced from the SFCC product record.

**Price**
- [ ] Given a shopper lands on a PDP and the product has a single full price, when the page loads, then the full price is displayed beneath the product name in the currency of the active storefront.

**Product description**
- [ ] Given a shopper lands on a PDP, when the page loads, then the product description is displayed.

**Product style code**
- [ ] Given a shopper lands on a PDP, when the page loads, then the product style code is displayed.

> *Optional input:*

**Model copy**
- [ ] Given a product has "Model is…" copy populated in the relevant SFCC attribute, when the page loads, then the model height and size worn are displayed on the page.
- [ ] Given a product does not have "Model is…" copy populated, when the page loads, then no model copy is displayed and no empty placeholder is shown.

---

**Breadcrumb navigation**
- [ ] Given a shopper is on a PDP, when the page loads, then a breadcrumb trail is displayed underneath the product pictures reflecting the product's category path (e.g. HOME / NEW / DRESSES / [PRODUCT NAME]).
- [ ] Given a shopper clicks a breadcrumb node, when the click is registered, then the shopper is navigated to the corresponding category page.

### Styling AC — held in two separate Jira Tasks, both still `To Do`

These are **not** subtasks of SFCC-89; they are standalone Tasks that name SFCC-89 in their body.
Both cite **Design ref: Figma node 5804-170721**.

**SFCC-732 — TC-001 — PDP Styling: Product Name Typography** (`Scope: Styling only`, precondition
1440px viewport):
- [ ] `.product-name` font-family = Futura Round
- [ ] `.product-name` font-size = 16px
- [ ] `.product-name` font-weight = 500
- [ ] `.product-name` line-height = 18px
- [ ] `.product-name` letter-spacing = -0.12px
- [ ] `.product-name` color = #191919
- [ ] `.product-name` text-transform = uppercase

**SFCC-733 — TC-002 — PDP Styling: Price Typography** (`Scope: Styling only`, precondition
"a PDP with a single full price" at 1440px):
- [ ] `.product-price` font-family = Futura Round
- [ ] `.product-price` font-size = 14px
- [ ] `.product-price` font-weight = 500
- [ ] `.product-price` line-height = 18px
- [ ] `.product-price` color = #191919

> Verified against the branch: the token values all line up. `heading3` = `fontSizes.xs` 16px /
> `fontWeights.medium` 500 / `lineHeights['2xs']` 18px / `letterSpacings.xs` -0.12px / uppercase, and
> `colour.ts` `text.default` = `grey[900]` = `#191919`. Price uses `--zimm-font-size-2xs` (14px),
> `--zimm-font-weight-medium`, `--zimm-font-lineheight-2xs` (18px), `text.default`.
> **The mismatch is the selector, not the value** — see Conflicts §6.5.

### Reference image (attachment)

One attachment: `image-20260716-035621.png` (482 KB, PNG, uploaded by Jasmijn Tsang 2026-07-16).
It is a **desktop PDP mock** — Zimmermann wordmark masthead over a full-bleed left-hand model shot,
right-hand info column showing (top to bottom): two tag pills (`RUNWAY`, `ANOTHER TAG`) with a
bookmark/wishlist icon at the right, product name `INDRA PLUNGE HALTER MAXI DRESS` in uppercase,
price `$1,100`, a short prose description, `Color: Raspberry` with two colour swatch thumbnails, a
`Size` dropdown with a `Find your size` link, a black full-width `ADD TO BAG` button, an underlined
`FIND IN BOUTIQUE` link, four `+` accordion rows (Details & Care / Size & Fit / Shipping & Returns /
Assistance), then `Model is 5'10" Tall/177cm and is wearing a US Size 6, runs true to size.` and
`Style Code: 7300JS261`.
**Important:** most of what the image shows is *out of scope* for SFCC-89. The description says
"Figma is leading". Only the name, price, description, model line and style code in that image belong
to this ticket. **No breadcrumb is visible in the attachment** — the crop ends above where it would sit.

---

## 3. IN SCOPE

From the description's own "In Scope" list (note: the list's **first bullet is literally empty** in
Jira — an authoring artifact, not a hidden requirement) plus the AC field:

1. **Product name** — from the SFCC product record, top of the product information panel.
2. **Full price** in the active storefront's currency — **single/full price only**.
3. **Product description**.
4. **"Model is…" copy** — model height and size worn. **Optional field**: must render nothing (not an
   empty placeholder) when unpopulated.
5. **Style Code**.
6. **Breadcrumb navigation** reflecting the product's category path, **at the bottom of the PDP /
   underneath the product pictures**, starting `HOME`, terminating in the product name, with each
   node navigating to its category page.

Implied-but-not-listed, and present in the branch's Gherkin (`e2e/features/pdp/SFCC-89_pdp-static-product-information.feature`):
loading skeletons, an error message when the product API fails, and graceful breadcrumb degradation
(Home-only) when the category API fails. **These are not in the Jira AC** — they are engineering
additions. Reasonable, but they are not a requirement anyone signed off; flagging so they aren't
mistaken for scope.

---

## 4. OUT OF SCOPE — and who owns it

Verbatim from SFCC-89's "Out of scope (separate stories)" list, mapped to the actual ticket:

| Excluded from SFCC-89 | Owning ticket | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Badges | **SFCC-132** PDP UI - Product Badges | **Blocked** |
| — badge merchandiser config | **SFCC-225** PDP – Product Badges — Merchandiser Configuration | Tech design |
| Was/Now sale price display | **SFCC-194** PDP – Was/Now Sale Price | Tech design |
| Wishlist icon (CTAs story) | **SFCC-434** PDP – Add to Wishlist | Tech design |
| — wishlist confirmation msg | **SFCC-710** PDP – Wishlist Confirmation Message on Add | To Do |
| Colour swatches & variation selection | **SFCC-91** PDP UI — Colour Swatches & Variation Selection | **In Progress** (same assignee) |
| — related colours attribute | **SFCC-708** PDP – Related Colours Attribute — BM / frontend | Tech design |
| Size selector & availability states | **SFCC-92** PDP — Size Selection & Add to Bag | **Blocked** |
| — product states (Coming Soon etc.) | **SFCC-150** PDP UI — Coming Soon, Back in Soon, Unavailable | **Blocked** |
| — buffer stock display | **SFCC-456** Buffer Stock – PDP Availability Display | To Do |
| Add to Bag CTA | **SFCC-92** | Blocked |
| Find in Boutique CTA | **SFCC-297** PDP UI — Find in Boutique Button and Slide-In Panel | Ready For Review |
| Image gallery | **SFCC-186** PDP – Product Image Gallery | Ready For Review |
| — gallery open/lightbox state | **SFCC-187** PDP – Image Gallery Open State | Tech design |
| — video in gallery | **SFCC-188** PDP – Product Video in Gallery | **Blocked** |
| Accordion — Details & Care | **SFCC-195** PDP – Slide Out - Details & Care | Tech design |
| Accordion — Size & Fit | **SFCC-102** PDP – Slide Out - Size & Fit | Ready For Review |
| Accordion — Shipping & Returns / Assistance | **SFCC-267** PDP – Slide Out – Shipping & Returns and Assistance | Ready For Review |
| Accordion — EU Environmental Qualities | **SFCC-266** PDP – Slide Out – EU Environmental Qualities | Ready For Review |
| Contentful-sourced content | (per-story; PDP has no Contentful story in this ticket) | — |

**Also out of scope, not named in SFCC-89's exclusion list but demonstrably owned elsewhere:**

- **Breadcrumb as a shared component** → **SFCC-578 SEO — Breadcrumb Component (PLP & PDP)**,
  epic **SFCC-22 SEO & Analytics & A/B Testing**, **Squad-B**, status **To Do**. See Conflicts §6.1.
- **BreadcrumbList structured data** → SFCC-573 (referenced by SFCC-578; depends on the component existing).
- Meta descriptions → SFCC-569 · hreflang → SFCC-564 · Product schema → SFCC-572 (all Squad-B, To Do).
- Measmerize / Find My Size → **SFCC-101** (Ready For Review).
- Max purchase qty → **SFCC-196** / **SFCC-268** / **SFCC-703**.
- Duties & taxes messaging → **SFCC-468**. Non-returnable badge → **SFCC-407**.
- Notify Me → **SFCC-149** / **SFCC-182** / **SFCC-183**.
- Gift card PDP → **SFCC-385** / **SFCC-386**.
- **PDP layout / hero composition** → **SFCC-723 `pdp/hero`** ("top-level orchestration component…
  composing `pdp/gallery` and `pdp/product-content` into a single responsive hero layout"). See §6.2.

---

## 5. Blockers and unresolved dependencies

### 5.1 Formal Jira links on SFCC-89

| Link | Ticket | Status | Blocking? |
|---|---|---|---|
| is blocked by | SFCC-205 Spike: Figma to React Setup | **Done** | No |
| is blocked by | SFCC-240 Spike: Figma-to-React Implementation Workflow | **Done** | No |
| is blocked by | **SFCC-26 Product Attributes – PDP** | **Ready to deploy to UAT** (Done category) | **Not Done in the environment** — see below |
| relates to | SFCC-132 PDP UI - Product Badges | **Blocked** | No (out of scope) |
| relates to | **SFCC-737 `pdp/product-content`** | Ready For Review | **Scope collision — see §6.2** |

**Subtasks:** SFCC-711 Test Case Creation — **Done**. SFCC-712 **Test Case Execution — To Do**.
SFCC-89 cannot honestly be called complete while SFCC-712 is unstarted.

### 5.2 SFCC-26 is "Ready to deploy to UAT", not deployed to the dev sandbox

SFCC-26 defines the product attribute schema SFCC-89 renders — including `name`, `shortDescription`,
`longDescription`, `styleNumber`, and critically **`modelFit`**. Its status sits in the *Done*
category but the status name is literally "Ready to **deploy** to UAT". Three E2E tests on the branch
are skipped with the note *"pending sandbox product provisioning"* (commit `4d7c129`), which is direct
evidence the attribute data is **not yet available in the environment SFCC-89 is being tested
against**. This is the single most material build blocker.

### 5.3 Design timing

Confluence **04.72 Component Design & User Story Tracker (id 408944644)** puts PDP at:
design components finalised **Aug 13 (Sprint 3)** · user stories ready for PO review **Aug 15** ·
**user stories ready for development Aug 24**. Today is **Aug 22**. SFCC-89 is already in Code Review,
i.e. **built ahead of its own "ready for development" date**. Confluence **04.7 Component Inventory
(id 400195591)** lists the PDP sub-component **"Product Content"** as **🟡 Done, minor update
required** — so the design SFCC-89 was built against is explicitly *not final*. 04.72 also states the
hard rule: *"Once a component is finalised and added to the UI kit, it is locked."* Product Content
is not yet locked.

### 5.4 Repo-level blockers introduced by the in-flight PR (governance, not requirements)

### 6.1 Breadcrumb ownership — SFCC-89 (Squad A) vs SFCC-578 (Squad B) — **highest risk**

SFCC-89 lists breadcrumb navigation as in-scope and has AC for it. **SFCC-578 "SEO — Breadcrumb
Component (PLP & PDP)"** is a *separate* story, in a *different epic* (SFCC-22 SEO & Analytics), owned
by a *different squad* (**Squad-B**), status **To Do**, describing the same component:
*"a breadcrumb navigation component displayed on PLP and PDP pages… BreadcrumbList schema (SFCC-573)
and heading hierarchy (SFCC-570) both depend on this component existing."*

The branch has already built `overrides/app/components/breadcrumb/index.tsx`. Per Confluence 04.72,
*"Each component is owned by the earliest epic in the sequence where it appears"* — which argues for
PDP owning it. But nobody has recorded that decision on either ticket, and SFCC-578 is still open and
unassigned. **Risk: Squad B builds a second breadcrumb, or SFCC-578 is closed without its SEO
requirements (BreadcrumbList schema, heading hierarchy) being met.** The current implementation emits
`<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">` + `<ol>` + `aria-current="page"` but **no JSON-LD / BreadcrumbList
structured data** — correctly so, since that is SFCC-572/573, but it means SFCC-578 is not satisfied
by this work.

Also note the **placement wording differs**: SFCC-89 says breadcrumb at the **bottom of the PDP** /
"underneath the product pictures"; SFCC-578 and the PLP designs treat breadcrumbs as a top-of-page
wayfinding element ("HOME / COLLECTIONS / SWIM AND RESORT"). `.docs/prd/pdp.md` §1 (PRD-001) says only
*"Breadcrumb navigation displayed on all PDP pages"* — no position. The AC is the more specific source
and says beneath the pictures; the branch follows the AC. Worth confirming PLP won't diverge.

### 6.2 Two live tickets claim the same static fields — SFCC-89 vs SFCC-737

- **SFCC-89** — Level 2 **page** story, epic **SFCC-5 (PDP)**, Squad A, **Code Review**.
- **SFCC-737 `pdp/product-content`** — Level 1 **component** story, epic **SFCC-2 (PWA Kit
  Components)**, **Ready For Review**, and its description says it covers *"the static content
  elements (**product name, description, model description, style code**) that are not extracted into
  separate components."*

That is verbatim SFCC-89's scope. The two are linked only as a soft "relates to". Confluence **04.71
Writing User Stories for Components (id 400195600)** is explicit that this must not happen:
Level 2 page stories *"should not repeat the component build detail from Level 1. They are about the
interaction between components and the end-to-end experience on that page."* By that rule the
**component build belongs to SFCC-737**, and SFCC-89 should be the page-assembly story. The work on
this branch has been done as a component build under SFCC-89. Someone must decide which ticket the
`pdpProductInfo` component actually satisfies, and whether SFCC-737 is now a duplicate.

Related: **SFCC-723 `pdp/hero`** owns *"layout and composition only… composing `pdp/gallery` and
`pdp/product-content`"*. The branch's `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` implements a
two-column grid with a gallery placeholder `<Box>` and a `PDP_OPTIONS_COLUMN_WIDTH = '360px'`
constant marked *"Provisional — no matching zimm token; pending designer sign-off"* — i.e. it is
doing `pdp/hero`'s job, with an unsigned-off magic value.

### 6.3 Model copy attribute — `modelFit` (spec) vs `c_sizeFit` (implementation) — **substantive**

This is a genuine requirements deviation, not a style nit.

**SFCC-26 (the blocking attribute story) defines two distinct attributes:**
- `modelFit` — *"This attribute is for displaying the model and sizing text **directly on the PDP**"* —
  sample: `Model is 5'10" Tall/177 cm and is wearing a US Size 6, runs true to size.`
- `sizeFit` — *"This attribute is for displaying the size and fit **on the Size & Fit tab**"* — which
  is **SFCC-102**, a different, out-of-scope story.

**The Jira comment history confirms `modelFit` was created deliberately for exactly this.**
Jasmijn Tsang, 2026-07-03: *"the model size and fit is now part of a overall 'size and fit' field in
Magento but in the new design we're taking the 'model' size and fit part to the PDP page — **that
requires a new product attribute which just contains that model size and fit part**. - To discuss with
Dani."* Then 2026-07-07: *"Informed them on product attribute needed for model size copy."*

**The branch does the opposite.** `overrides/app/utils/productData.ts` regex-scrapes the model line
out of the *Size & Fit* HTML:

```ts
/** Extracts the plain-text content of the first <li> starting with "Model is"
 *  from a sizeFit HTML string (SFCC c_sizeFit attribute). */
export function extractModelLine(html: string | undefined): string | undefined {
  if (!html) return undefined;
  const match = html.match(/<li>\s*(Model is[^<]*?)\s*<\/li>/i);
  return match?.[1]?.trim() || undefined;
}
```

…and `product-detail/index.tsx` calls `extractModelLine((product as ProductWithSizeFit)?.c_sizeFit)`.

This is the pre-decision Magento behaviour the business explicitly moved away from. It is also brittle
(English-only `"Model is"` match, in an 11-locale storefront; breaks on any markup or copy variation)
and it silently couples SFCC-89 to SFCC-102's attribute. **Either `c_modelFit` is not yet provisioned
in the sandbox — which makes this a temporary workaround that must be flagged and removed — or the
requirement changed and nobody updated SFCC-26.** Must be confirmed with Jasmijn/Dani before sign-off.

id, which is the stylecode, is displayed on the PDP**"* and *"`styleNumber` — This attribute is
**always** the master product id, whereas the product-id attribute can also contain the colour variant

**Subtasks:** SFCC-711 Test Case Creation — **Done**. SFCC-712 **Test Case Execution — To Do**.
SFCC-89 cannot honestly be called complete while SFCC-712 is unstarted.

### 5.2 SFCC-26 is "Ready to deploy to UAT", not deployed to the dev sandbox

SFCC-26 defines the product attribute schema SFCC-89 renders — including `name`, `shortDescription`,
`longDescription`, `styleNumber`, and critically **`modelFit`**. Its status sits in the *Done*
category but the status name is literally "Ready to **deploy** to UAT". Three E2E tests on the branch
are skipped with the note *"pending sandbox product provisioning"* (commit `4d7c129`), which is direct
evidence the attribute data is **not yet available in the environment SFCC-89 is being tested
against**. This is the single most material build blocker.

### 5.3 Design timing

Confluence **04.72 Component Design & User Story Tracker (id 408944644)** puts PDP at:
design components finalised **Aug 13 (Sprint 3)** · user stories ready for PO review **Aug 15** ·
**user stories ready for development Aug 24**. Today is **Aug 22**. SFCC-89 is already in Code Review,
i.e. **built ahead of its own "ready for development" date**. Confluence **04.7 Component Inventory
(id 400195591)** lists the PDP sub-component **"Product Content"** as **🟡 Done, minor update
required** — so the design SFCC-89 was built against is explicitly *not final*. 04.72 also states the
hard rule: *"Once a component is finalised and added to the UI kit, it is locked."* Product Content
is not yet locked.

### 5.4 Repo-level blockers introduced by the in-flight PR (governance, not requirements)

Cross-checked against `git diff develop...HEAD`:

  `package-lock.json`). `package.json (root)` is **Tier 1 / frozen** (`.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`)
  **and** AGENTS.md Hard Rule #7 forbids adding packages without integration-team approval. There is

  (`protectedFiles.md`), requires a non-author review.
- **`overrides/app/theme/components/`** (new `pdpProductInfo.ts` + `index.ts` registration) — **Tier 2**,
  owner *UI Designer, notify before changing*.
- Touching Tier 1 and Tier 2 in one change trips **Hard Rule #10** (never touch more than one
  protection tier without confirming scope).

### 5.5 PR linkage

**Jira's development panel is empty** — no PRs, branches, or commits. The only pointer to the PR is a
comment: *"This card is already ready for review: https://github.com/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/pull/57"*
(Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz, 2026-08-19). The Jira dev integration is configured for **Bitbucket**, but the
repo is on **GitHub** — so dev-panel traceability for this ticket does not work and shouldn't be relied on.

## 6. Conflicts between sources

> Project rule (AGENTS.md > Requirements): confirmed PRDs are the source of truth; conflicts must be
> surfaced, not silently resolved. Each of the following needs a human decision.

### 6.1 Breadcrumb ownership — SFCC-89 (Squad A) vs SFCC-578 (Squad B) — **highest risk**

SFCC-89 lists breadcrumb navigation as in-scope and has AC for it. **SFCC-578 "SEO — Breadcrumb
Component (PLP & PDP)"** is a *separate* story, in a *different epic* (SFCC-22 SEO & Analytics), owned
by a *different squad* (**Squad-B**), status **To Do**, describing the same component:
*"a breadcrumb navigation component displayed on PLP and PDP pages… BreadcrumbList schema (SFCC-573)
and heading hierarchy (SFCC-570) both depend on this component existing."*

The branch has already built `overrides/app/components/breadcrumb/index.tsx`. Per Confluence 04.72,
*"Each component is owned by the earliest epic in the sequence where it appears"* — which argues for
PDP owning it. But nobody has recorded that decision on either ticket, and SFCC-578 is still open and
unassigned. **Risk: Squad B builds a second breadcrumb, or SFCC-578 is closed without its SEO
requirements (BreadcrumbList schema, heading hierarchy) being met.** The current implementation emits
`<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">` + `<ol>` + `aria-current="page"` but **no JSON-LD / BreadcrumbList
structured data** — correctly so, since that is SFCC-572/573, but it means SFCC-578 is not satisfied
by this work.

Also note the **placement wording differs**: SFCC-89 says breadcrumb at the **bottom of the PDP** /
"underneath the product pictures"; SFCC-578 and the PLP designs treat breadcrumbs as a top-of-page
wayfinding element ("HOME / COLLECTIONS / SWIM AND RESORT"). `.docs/prd/pdp.md` §1 (PRD-001) says only
*"Breadcrumb navigation displayed on all PDP pages"* — no position. The AC is the more specific source
and says beneath the pictures; the branch follows the AC. Worth confirming PLP won't diverge.

### 6.2 Two live tickets claim the same static fields — SFCC-89 vs SFCC-737

- **SFCC-89** — Level 2 **page** story, epic **SFCC-5 (PDP)**, Squad A, **Code Review**.
- **SFCC-737 `pdp/product-content`** — Level 1 **component** story, epic **SFCC-2 (PWA Kit
  Components)**, **Ready For Review**, and its description says it covers *"the static content
  elements (**product name, description, model description, style code**) that are not extracted into
  separate components."*

That is verbatim SFCC-89's scope. The two are linked only as a soft "relates to". Confluence **04.71
Writing User Stories for Components (id 400195600)** is explicit that this must not happen:
Level 2 page stories *"should not repeat the component build detail from Level 1. They are about the
interaction between components and the end-to-end experience on that page."* By that rule the
**component build belongs to SFCC-737**, and SFCC-89 should be the page-assembly story. The work on
this branch has been done as a component build under SFCC-89. Someone must decide which ticket the
`pdpProductInfo` component actually satisfies, and whether SFCC-737 is now a duplicate.

Related: **SFCC-723 `pdp/hero`** owns *"layout and composition only… composing `pdp/gallery` and
`pdp/product-content`"*. The branch's `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` implements a
two-column grid with a gallery placeholder `<Box>` and a `PDP_OPTIONS_COLUMN_WIDTH = '360px'`
constant marked *"Provisional — no matching zimm token; pending designer sign-off"* — i.e. it is
doing `pdp/hero`'s job, with an unsigned-off magic value.

### 6.3 Model copy attribute — `modelFit` (spec) vs `c_sizeFit` (implementation) — **substantive**

This is a genuine requirements deviation, not a style nit.

**SFCC-26 (the blocking attribute story) defines two distinct attributes:**
- `modelFit` — *"This attribute is for displaying the model and sizing text **directly on the PDP**"* —
  sample: `Model is 5'10" Tall/177 cm and is wearing a US Size 6, runs true to size.`
- `sizeFit` — *"This attribute is for displaying the size and fit **on the Size & Fit tab**"* — which
  is **SFCC-102**, a different, out-of-scope story.

**The Jira comment history confirms `modelFit` was created deliberately for exactly this.**
Jasmijn Tsang, 2026-07-03: *"the model size and fit is now part of a overall 'size and fit' field in
Magento but in the new design we're taking the 'model' size and fit part to the PDP page — **that
requires a new product attribute which just contains that model size and fit part**. - To discuss with
Dani."* Then 2026-07-07: *"Informed them on product attribute needed for model size copy."*

**The branch does the opposite.** `overrides/app/utils/productData.ts` regex-scrapes the model line
out of the *Size & Fit* HTML:

```ts
/** Extracts the plain-text content of the first <li> starting with "Model is"
 *  from a sizeFit HTML string (SFCC c_sizeFit attribute). */
export function extractModelLine(html: string | undefined): string | undefined {
  if (!html) return undefined;
  const match = html.match(/<li>\s*(Model is[^<]*?)\s*<\/li>/i);
  return match?.[1]?.trim() || undefined;
}
```

…and `product-detail/index.tsx` calls `extractModelLine((product as ProductWithSizeFit)?.c_sizeFit)`.

This is the pre-decision Magento behaviour the business explicitly moved away from. It is also brittle
(English-only `"Model is"` match, in an 11-locale storefront; breaks on any markup or copy variation)
and it silently couples SFCC-89 to SFCC-102's attribute. **Either `c_modelFit` is not yet provisioned
in the sandbox — which makes this a temporary workaround that must be flagged and removed — or the
requirement changed and nobody updated SFCC-26.** Must be confirmed with Jasmijn/Dani before sign-off.

### 6.4 Style code source — `product.id` vs `styleNumber`

SFCC-26 is precise: *"`ID` … can be the master product id / variant product id. **The master product
id, which is the stylecode, is displayed on the PDP**"* and *"`styleNumber` — This attribute is
**always** the master product id, whereas the product-id attribute can also contain the colour variant
or size variant ID."* The branch passes `styleCode={product?.id}`. On a master-product URL that is
correct; **once SFCC-91 (colour swatches, currently In Progress) starts routing to colour-variant IDs,
`product.id` will render a variant ID where the style code should be.** Sample values from SFCC-26:
`4673TS251` (style code) vs `4673TS251GVSCP0P` (variant). Low effort to fix now, latent bug if left.

### 6.5 Styling test cases assert CSS selectors the implementation does not expose

SFCC-732/733 assert on `.product-name` and `.product-price`. The component exposes neither — it uses
Chakra `__css` with `data-testid="product-price"` and no testid or class on the name element at all.
The *values* match (verified in §2), but both test cases will fail as written. Since SFCC-712 (Test
Case Execution) is still To Do, this will surface at QA. Needs a dev/QA agreement on the selector
contract.

### 6.6 `.docs/prd/pdp.md` vs Confluence 04.1.8 — two struck-through requirements

`.docs/prd/pdp.md` §13 documents **PRD-023 ("As Seen" editorial module)** and **PRD-025 (Styling
module)** as *"confirmed"*. Confluence **04.1.8 (id 302776322)** — which states it was extracted from
the functional-requirements workbook after all requirements were confirmed — shows **both rows struck
through, i.e. out of scope**: PRD-023 *"replaced by new ones designed (Shop the edit, Complete the
look, More from Category)"*; PRD-025 *"not having this anymore"*. The local PRD mirror is **stale**.
Does not affect SFCC-89 (both are out of scope either way) but the file is being treated as a source
of truth for other PDP stories and will mislead.

`.docs/prd/pdp.md` is **consistent** with SFCC-89 on everything in scope: §1 breadcrumb on all PDPs
(PRD-001) and style code (PRD-007); §2 name/price from Product API (PRD-002); §5 price in storefront
currency. No conflict found there.

### 6.7 `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` is stale and contradicts Jira

The file is self-labelled *"Draft (2026-06-23)"* and says **"Current position: Sprint 0 — Foundation
(in progress)"**. It maps **Sprint 3 = 27 Jul – 7 Aug** with *"PDP (Part 2)"*. Jira's real
**SFCC Sprint 3 = 10 Aug – 24 Aug 2026** (active, board 500), which is where SFCC-89 actually sits.
Per AGENTS.md Hard Rule #14 this file is supposed to be checked before scoping new work — as written
it would give the wrong sprint and the wrong "what exists yet" picture. Do not rely on it.

`.docs/memory/projectState.md` contains **no SFCC-89, PDP-build, or breadcrumb entry at all** — only
three passing mentions of PDP in forward-looking lists. There is no local record of this work.

   already uses. This is a **varying** residual (other styles match exactly), so per the project's
   own rule it is a real defect, not a measurement artifact.
2. **Product name uses a different style on mobile than desktop** — `Default/Heading 3` (−1% =
   −0.16px) vs `Default/h3-strong` (−0.12px absolute). Same family/size/line-height/case. This is a
   **designer decision to confirm**, not something to silently pick a winner for. The repo has only
   `heading3` (−0.12px), which matches desktop.

### ⚠️ The Desktop/Mobile variable modes are a trap — do not implement them

The design-system `Typography` collection is **mode-switched**, and several sizes differ:

| Variable | Desktop | Mobile |
|---|---|---|
| `default/body-2` | 14 | **12** |
| `default/body-2 medium` | 14 | **12** |
| `default/caption` | 12 | 12 |
| `default/button` | 14 | 14 |
| `line-height/heading-3-medium` | 18 | 18 |
| `line-height/body-2 medium` | 18 | 18 |
| `line-height/caption` | 16 | 16 |
| `line-height/product names` | 16 | 16 |

**But the 402 mobile frame does not switch to the Mobile mode.** Both `3093:67151` (1440) and
`3093:67195` (402) resolve the Typography collection to the *same* mode id (`1226:10`), and no node
in either subtree sets an explicit mode. **Measured consequence: every rendered font size is
identical on both breakpoints (16 / 14 / 12).**

So: implement a **single** type scale. Do **not** add a responsive `fontSize` step for body-2 on the
strength of the mode existing. Whether mobile body text *should* be 12px is an unresolved
**designer question** — the tokens say one thing and the composed screens say another.

---

## 4. Colour spec

Every colour variable bound in this node reports **`remote: true`** — they resolve from the
**subscribed design-system library**, not this file. (This file *also* contains local collections
named `Typography`/`Spacing`/`Colour`/`Grid`; which is canonical is worth confirming, but the
bindings in use are the remote ones. Per the brief, the DS file is `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm`.)

| Figma variable | Collection | Value | Repo token | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `text/default` | Colour | `#191919` | `colors.text.default` (`grey[900]`) | ✅ exact |
| `alias/color/text/default` | Alias | ALIAS → `#191919` | `colors.text.default` | ✅ exact (see note) |
| `text/secondary` | Colour | `#666666` | `colors.text.secondary` (`grey[600]`) | ✅ exact |
| `text/inverse` | Colour | `#ffffff` | `colors.text.inverse` (`grey.white`) | ✅ exact |
| `button/default` | Colour | `#191919` | `colors.action.primary.bgDefault` (`grey[900]`) | ✅ exact |

**Unbound raw colours in the design (no variable attached):**

| Raw value | Where | Repo token with the same value | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `#f6f4f1` | swatch background rects `5083:70374`, `5083:70377` | `ivory[200]` / `colors.background['02']` | ✅ value matches — but **unbound in Figma** |
| `#ffffff` | size-selector chevron backing `5083:70386` | `grey.white` / `colors.background['07']` | ✅ value matches — unbound |
| **`#000000`** | "Size Guide" `5083:70372`, "Find your size" `5083:70390` / `5083:70474` | **none** | ❌ **NO MATCH — see below** |

**⚠️ `#000000` is almost certainly a design defect.** Every other text node in the column is
`text/default` `#191919`. Two labels use pure black with no variable bound. The repo has no
`#000000` text token (`grey.black: 'black'` exists as a primitive but no semantic alias maps to it,
and `text.default` is `#191919`). **Do not invent a token and do not silently substitute
`text.default`** — ask the UI designer whether these should be `text/default`.

**Note on the two text-default variables:** `alias/color/text/default` (Alias collection) and
`text/default` (Colour collection) both resolve to `#191919` and are used on sibling nodes within
the same column. That is a design-system inconsistency, not a repo problem — both map to the single
repo token `colors.text.default`.

Borders/strokes: size-selector rule `5083:70388` is `1px` `text/default` `#191919` → repo
`borderWidths.default` (`1px`) + `colors.text.default`. ✅ Button container carries a `1px`
`button/default` stroke identical to its fill (visually invisible; likely there so the Secondary
variant can swap it).

---

## 5. Spacing spec

The design-system `Spacing` collection is **identical to the repo's `spacing.ts` scale**:

```
section/3xs=2  2xs=4  xs=8  s=12  m=16  l=20  xl=24  2xl=32  3xl=40  4xl=64  5xl=80  6xl=128  7xl=160
```
Repo: `3xs 2 · 2xs 4 · xs 8 · s 12 · m 16 · l 20 · xl 24 · 2xl 32 · 3xl 40 · 4xl 64 · 5xl 80 · 6xl 128 · 7xl 160` — **1:1 exact match.**
(The DS also has `gap-1=24`, `gap-2=16`, with no repo counterpart — but nothing in this node binds them.)

| Measured value | Where | Repo token | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **2** | accordion wrapper gap `5083:70396/97` | `spacing['3xs']` | ✅ |
| **4** | wishlist icon padding (bound to `alias/space/100`) | `spacing['2xs']` | ✅ |
| **8** | swatch block gap; FIND IN BOUTIQUE row gap | `spacing.xs` | ✅ |
| **16** | CTA gap, accordion list gap, accordion label↔icon gap | `spacing.m` | ✅ |
| **24** | button padding-X | `spacing.xl` | ✅ |
| **30** | mobile side gutter | `grid.containerPadding.base` (`'30px'`) — DS `grid-margin` Mobile | ✅ |
| **80** | mobile info block padding-bottom | `spacing['5xl']` | ✅ |
| **5** | button padding-Y | ❌ none — but equals `BTN_PADDING_Y` in `button.ts` | ⚠️ known provisional |
| **6** | name wrapper padding-top `5083:70428` | ❌ none (4 / 8 bracket it) | **GAP** |
| **15** | colour label ↔ "Size Guide" | ❌ none (12 / 16 bracket it) | **GAP** |
| **22** | within title block | ❌ none (20 / 24 bracket it) | **GAP** |
| **28** | info column stack gap | ❌ none (24 / 32 bracket it) | **GAP** |
| **43** | name ↔ wishlist | ❌ none — treat as space-between | **GAP / inference** |
| **44** | title group ↔ swatch group | ❌ none (40 / 64 bracket it) | **GAP** |
| **142** | desktop right padding | ❌ none | **GAP** |
| **179** | gallery ↔ info column gap | ❌ none | **GAP** |

**Only one spacing value in the entire column is bound to a variable** (`alias/space/100` = 4px on
the wishlist icon padding). Every other gap and pad is a **raw literal typed into the layer**. Six of
them (6, 15, 22, 28, 43, 44) are **off the design system's own scale** — so these are not "the repo
is missing a token", they are values that don't exist in the DS either. That is a **designer
decision**, not something to round to the nearest token silently.

### Sizes

| Measured | Where | Repo token | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Button height **50** | both breakpoints | `BTN_HEIGHT_LG` = `'50px'` | ✅ **design corroborates `button.ts`** |
| Button padding **24 / 5** | both breakpoints | `px: var(--zimm-scale-xl)` (24), `BTN_PADDING_Y` (5) | ✅ exact |
| — | — | `actionSizes.height.lg` = `'52px'`, `paddingX.lg` = `'32px'` | ❌ **contradicted by the design** |
| Wishlist glyph **16** (desktop) | `5083:70430` | `iconSizes.md` (`16px`) | ✅ |
| Wishlist icon **20** (mobile) | `5083:70448` | `iconSizes.lg` (`20px`) | ✅ but ⚠️ differs from desktop |
| Accordion chevron **9** | ×4 both breakpoints | ❌ none (`iconSizes.sm` = 12) | **GAP** |
| Size chevron **9** desktop / **13** mobile | `70386` / `70470` | ❌ none | **GAP + inconsistency** |

**This resolves a standing open item in the repo.** `overrideStyling.md` records that
`BTN_HEIGHT_LG` (50px) and `BTN_PADDING_Y` (5px) are provisional prototype values pending
UI-designer sign-off, and that they disagree with `actionSizes` (52px / 32px). **This design measures
50 / 5 / 24 on a CSS-comparable INSTANCE at both breakpoints** — i.e. the values already in
`button.ts` are the ones the approved design uses, and `actionSizes` is the outlier. Worth taking
back to the designer to close the item; it is not licence to edit `sizes.ts` (Tier 1).

---

## 6. Responsive variants found

**Measured — frame widths present on this PDP page:**

| Width | Count | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **1440** | ~15 frames | `PDP 01`, `PDP - INDRA … Desktop - Size`, `PDP - Details and care`, `Carousel 4–7` |
| **402** | ~12 frames | `PDP 01 Mob`, `ALCHEMY … Mobile`, `PDP - Details and Care Mob` |
| 1920 x 1080 | 1 | frame named `-` — presentation backdrop, not a storefront breakpoint |
| 1176, 753, 101, 218… | several | annotation chips, `PDP animation`, label pills — not screens |

> **There is no 1023-width frame anywhere on this page.** The brief anticipated 402 / 1023 / 1440;
> only **402 and 1440** exist for the PDP. Tablet is undesigned here.

### ⚠️ FRAME WIDTH IS NOT A BREAKPOINT

The repo's actual breakpoints (`overrides/app/theme/foundation/gridSystem.ts`, registered in
`theme/index.ts`):

```
base 0em · sm 30em (NOT used) · md 48em = 768px · lg 62em (NOT used) · xl 80em = 1280px · 2xl 96em (NOT used)
```

There is **no 860 or 1024 breakpoint token in the theme** (grepped: zero hits for `860`). If the
brief's "768 / 860 / 1024" came from somewhere else, it is not the Chakra breakpoint scale.

Mapping **402 → `base`** and **1440 → `xl`** is a **decision to be confirmed, not a measured fact.**

**The real gap: the 768–1280 range (`md`) is undesigned for this column.** The design jumps from a
342 px full-bleed mobile block to a fixed 218 px desktop column beside a 900 px gallery. Nothing
specifies what happens in between. Note that the DS `Grid` collection *does* define a Tablet mode
(`grid-columns` 8, `grid-margin` 24, matching the repo's `md` values) — so tablet is tokenised but
not drawn. **This needs a designer answer before implementation.**

### Bonus finding (outside PDP scope, flagged not actioned)

The DS `Grid` collection defines `grid-gutter` = **Desktop 1 / Tablet 24 / Mobile 30**. The repo's
`gridSystem.ts` hardcodes a single `columnGap: '1px'` for all breakpoints and its comment asserts
"1px gutter" at every tier. If `grid-gutter` means column gap, the repo is correct only at desktop.
`gridSystem.ts` is **Tier 1** — do not touch; raise with the UI designer. Columns (10/8/4) and
margins (0/24/30) match the repo exactly.

---

## 7. TOKEN GAPS — need a UI-designer decision (do not invent values)

Ordered by how likely they are to block implementation.

**A. Off-scale spacing values (6 of them).** `6`, `15`, `22`, `28`, `43`, `44` px are not in the
repo's scale *nor* in the design system's own `Spacing` collection. `28` (the main column rhythm) and
`44` (the largest structural gap) are the important ones. Ask: round to `xl`/`2xl` (24/32) and
`3xl` (40), or add new tokens?

**B. Undesigned tablet (768–1280).** No 1023-ish frame exists. Column behaviour between 342-full-bleed
and 218-fixed is unspecified. Blocking for a responsive implementation.

**C. `#000000` on two labels.** "Size Guide" and "Find your size" use unbound pure black while
everything else uses `text/default` `#191919`. No repo token matches. Almost certainly a design slip.

**D. Product name style differs by breakpoint.** `Default/h3-strong` (−0.12px) desktop vs
`Default/Heading 3` (−0.16px) mobile. Pick one.

**E. `body2Strong` letter-spacing is −0.12px in the repo but −0.14px in Figma.** Unlike the others
this has an unambiguous fix — `letterSpacings['2xs']` already exists and is exactly −0.14px. Still a
Tier 1 file (`typography.ts`), so it needs the designer/owner, but it is a defect not a gap.

**F. Icon sizes with no token.** Accordion chevron `9 x 9` (×4, both breakpoints) and the size
chevron (`9` desktop / `13` mobile). `iconSizes` only has 20/16/12. The 9/13 split between
breakpoints looks unintentional.

**G. Wishlist icon differs by breakpoint** — 16px glyph desktop (in a 24px 4-padded tappable box)
vs bare 20px mobile. Both map to existing tokens, but the mobile one has **no padding**, giving a
20 x 20 hit target — **below the WCAG 2.2 AA 24 x 24 minimum target size (2.5.8)**. Flag to design.

**H. Unbound brand colours.** `#f6f4f1` and `#ffffff` match repo tokens by value but carry no Figma
variable, so they will drift. Cosmetic in the DS, no repo action.

**I. Component dimensions with no token** — gallery `900 x 1170`, swatch `55 x 72` / `56 x 72`,
desktop info column `218`, gallery↔column gap `179`, right pad `142`. Expected for a composed page;
listed for completeness.

**J. The swatch block stays 216 px wide on a 342 px mobile column.** Confirm intentional.

---

## 8. Cross-reference summary

**Matches the repo exactly (no action):** `heading3`, `price`, `body2`, `caption`, `linkLg`,
`linkSm`, `button` text styles · `text.default`, `text.secondary`, `text.inverse`,
`action.primary.bgDefault` colours · spacing `2/4/8/16/24/80` · mobile `30px` gutter ·
`borderWidths.default` · the whole DS spacing scale · grid columns and margins.

**Corroborates a repo open item:** button `50 / 5 / 24` confirms `button.ts`'s provisional constants
and contradicts `actionSizes` (52 / 32).

**Genuine defects found:** `body2Strong` letter-spacing (−0.12 vs −0.14px); `#000000` on two labels;
product-name style differs by breakpoint; mobile wishlist target 20 x 20 < WCAG 2.2 AA 24 x 24;
`grid-gutter` tablet/mobile values absent from `gridSystem.ts`; layer named `Size & Fit` renders
`Details & Care`.

**Uniform vs varying residuals:** no uniform offset was observed anywhere — matching values matched
*exactly* (0 px residual). Every discrepancy listed is therefore a **varying** residual and, per the
project's own rule, a real defect rather than a measurement artifact.

**Source file:** `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` (Zimmermann_Final-Approved-Designs) — composed page states.
**Target node given:** `3087:15747`.
**Extracted:** 2026-08-22. Read-only; no repo file and no Figma node was modified.

---

## 0. Method and tool caveats (read this before trusting any number)

Two of the four requested tools were **unusable in this session**:

| Tool | Result |
|---|---|
| `get_metadata` (with nodeId) | Works, but the target subtree serialises to >315 KB and the MCP SSE transport truncates it. **Deterministic failure**, retried twice. |
| `get_screenshot` | Works. Used throughout. |
| `get_variable_defs` | **Fails**: `"You currently have nothing selected."` It resolves against the Figma **desktop app's current selection**, not the `nodeId` argument. |
| `get_design_context` | **Fails**: same "nothing selected" error, same reason. |

Because `get_variable_defs` and `get_design_context` were unavailable, all variable, typography and
layout data below was obtained instead via **read-only Plugin API traversal** (`use_figma` with
scripts that only read and `return`). This is a *better* source than `get_design_context` for this
purpose — it returns resolved variable names, collections, modes and per-mode values rather than
pre-rendered Tailwind — but it is a substitution worth stating.

**If you want `get_design_context` / `get_variable_defs` output**, the user must select the node in
the Figma desktop app first; nothing in this environment can do that.

Two further transport quirks, recorded so the next person doesn't rediscover them:
- The SSE channel truncates responses at a **variable** cap (~19 KB–315 KB observed). All traversal
  was paginated.
- **A non-ASCII character in some layer names breaks the SSE JSON encoding outright** (frames named
  `PDP - Denim Applique<U+?>Mini Dress`). Every script below sanitises names to ASCII. A script that
  returns raw `node.name` for that range fails 100% of the time.

### Measurement rules applied

- **TEXT nodes report a cap-height box, not a CSS line box.** Every TEXT height below is labelled
  and must **not** be turned into a CSS `height` or used to file a mismatch.
- **A FRAME that hugs a TEXT child inherits that cap-height artifact.** This bites here: the
  accordion row frames report `218x9`. That 9 px is the text cap-height, not a row height. For those,
  use the **row pitch** (gap + measured offsets), which is artifact-free.
- FRAMEs/INSTANCEs with fixed or content-independent sizing (column widths, button, icons, gallery)
  report real boxes and **are** directly CSS-comparable.

---

## 1. What this screen is, and the node tree

**`3087:15747` is not a screen — it is a `PAGE`** named `└– 🟢  PDP`, containing **67 top-level
children** and spanning 108649 × 41878 px of canvas. The green marker in the page name appears to be
this file's "approved" convention (unverified — a naming convention, not metadata).

The 67 children are the whole PDP design surface: base layouts, three product variants
(INDRA PLUNGE HALTER MAXI DRESS, ALCHEMY RUFFLE MINI DRESS, Denim Applique Mini Dress), interaction
states, plus `SECTION`s named `archive`, `archived - not needed`, `Archive`,
`Out of stock / coming soon`, `Size selection (drop down interaction)`, `Mobile sticky add to bag`
and `Shop the look mockups`.

## 2. Layout spec

this has an unambiguous fix — `letterSpacings['2xs']` already exists and is exactly −0.14px. Still a
Tier 1 file (`typography.ts`), so it needs the designer/owner, but it is a defect not a gap.

**F. Icon sizes with no token.** Accordion chevron `9 x 9` (×4, both breakpoints) and the size
chevron (`9` desktop / `13` mobile). `iconSizes` only has 20/16/12. The 9/13 split between
breakpoints looks unintentional.

**G. Wishlist icon differs by breakpoint** — 16px glyph desktop (in a 24px 4-padded tappable box)
vs bare 20px mobile. Both map to existing tokens, but the mobile one has **no padding**, giving a
20 x 20 hit target — **below the WCAG 2.2 AA 24 x 24 minimum target size (2.5.8)**. Flag to design.

**H. Unbound brand colours.** `#f6f4f1` and `#ffffff` match repo tokens by value but carry no Figma
variable, so they will drift. Cosmetic in the DS, no repo action.

**I. Component dimensions with no token** — gallery `900 x 1170`, swatch `55 x 72` / `56 x 72`,
desktop info column `218`, gallery↔column gap `179`, right pad `142`. Expected for a composed page;
listed for completeness.

---

## 2. What a new PDP component must look like structurally

### 2a. The naming families — keep them straight

| Family | Case | Where | Live examples on this branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| SFCC override dirs (shadow a base module) | **kebab-case**, matching the base filename exactly | `overrides/app/components/<kebab>/` | `breadcrumb/`, `header/`, `icons/`, `_app-config/` |
| Zimmermann-authored components | **camelCase** | `overrides/app/components/<camel>/` or `ui-kits/<tier>/<camel>/` | `pdpProductInfo/`, `pageContainer/`, `button/`, `ui-kits/atoms/zimmPageToolbar/` |
| SFCC `shared/ui` primitives | **PascalCase** | `node_modules/…/app/components/shared/ui/<Pascal>/` | `Box/`, `Text/`, `Skeleton/` — thin re-exports of Chakra |

Rule source: `.claude/rules/conventions.md` > File naming and folder structure. **[V]**

### 2b. What `ui-kits/` actually contains today

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/
└── atoms/
    ├── .gitkeep
    └── zimmPageToolbar/
        ├── index.tsx
        └── index.stories.tsx
```

**One component. No `molecules/`, no `organisms/` directories exist.** **[V]**

### 2c. Where the `ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}` convention is written down — and the problem

Grepping the whole repo for `ui-kits` on this branch returns **three hits**: two imports in the PDP
page/story, and one row in the generated registry. **There is no rules doc on this branch or on
`develop` that states the ui-kits convention.** **[V]**

The doc exists only on an unmerged branch: `.claude/rules/uikit-components.md`, 512 lines, on
`origin/feature/f2r-implementation-workflow` (last commit 2026-08-11). **[V]**

**That doc contradicts the styling rules on `develop`.** Read side by side **[V]**:

| `.claude/rules/uikit-components.md` (f2r-implementation-workflow, unmerged) | `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` (on `develop` since `5b36062`, 2026-08-18) |
|---|---|
| "`import { Box, Flex, Text, … } from '@chakra-ui/react'` is **forbidden** inside `ui-kits/{tier}/{component}/`" | Hierarchy level 1–3 is Chakra `textStyle` props, semantic token strings, then a `theme/components/<name>.ts` config |
| Co-located `{component}.styles.ts` + Emotion `<Global styles={…}/>` per component; "There is no fallback." | "`.zimm-*` classes remain the right tool for genuinely static, non-interactive… treatments"; a class mirror of an interactive component is "structurally incomplete from the start" |
| Handover CSS class names via `className`, inline `style={{color:'var(--zimm-color-…)'}}` | "**Never**: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file"; theme config is "the single source of truth" |

`f2r-implementation-workflow` does **not** contain `overrideStyling.md` at all — the two rule sets are
mutually exclusive, living on different branches. The newer `origin/feature/f2r-component-registry`
(2026-08-21, 27 commits ahead, `develop` **is** its ancestor) carries `overrideStyling.md` **and** adds
`.claude/rules/overrides.md`, but **not** `uikit-components.md`. **[V]**

**[I]** Reading recency: `overrideStyling.md` (Aug 18, on develop) supersedes `uikit-components.md`
(Aug 11, unmerged), and the surviving f2r branch dropped the latter. Treat `overrideStyling.md` as
authoritative. **This is a judgement call that should be confirmed with the developer** before a

The last two commits (`3e1686b`, `d526ad1`) are the author *starting* to migrate styling into theme recipes — that migration was done for `PdpProductInfo` only and never applied to `Breadcrumb`, `ZimmPageToolbar`, or the page itself. 72:| `overrides/app/components/breadcrumb/index.stories.tsx` | 77 | `Layout/Breadcrumb`, 4 stories + `play` |
105:- **Renders:** a two-column grid — a grey placeholder `<Box>` where the image gallery belongs, and an options column containing `PdpProductInfo`; below it a `ZimmPageToolbar variant="breadcrumbs"` wrapping `Breadcrumb`.

199:- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/product-list/partials/page-header.jsx:20` → `<Breadcrumb categories={category.parentCategoryTree} />` (**the PLP breadcrumb**)
207:| `className="sf-breadcrumb"`, `data-testid="sf-crumb-item"` | neither | any selector keyed on these breaks (none in-repo today) |
208:| `useStyleConfig('Breadcrumb')` — theme-driven | styles hardcoded in the component (`index.tsx:22-35`) | breaks the branch's own theme-recipe pattern |
209:| `<ChevronRightIcon>` separator | literal `/` text (`index.tsx:39`) | **PLP breadcrumb visual changes**, unreviewed by design |
210:| Chakra `Breadcrumb`/`BreadcrumbItem`/`BreadcrumbLink` | raw `Box`/`Text` | loses Chakra's breadcrumb a11y primitives |
215:CodeRabbit flagged the related import issue at `breadcrumb/index.tsx:4` (Major, still open): the file imports `Box, Text` from `@chakra-ui/react` while the rest of the codebase (`zimmPageToolbar/index.tsx:3`, `product-detail/index.tsx:5`) uses `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui`. Inconsistent, and per the `shared/ui` barrel behaviour this bypasses the project's own UI surface.
225:| `overrides/app/components/breadcrumb/index.tsx:33` | `transition: 'opacity var(--zimm-motion-duration-fast) var(--zimm-motion-easing-standard)'` |
236:Additionally: `overrides/app/components/breadcrumb/index.tsx:22-35` hardcodes `BASE_STYLE`/`LINK_PROPS` objects in the component rather than a theme recipe, and `zimmPageToolbar/index.tsx:28-33` hardcodes a `PADDING` map. Both are level-3 candidates (own theme config) per `overrideStyling.md`. Neither has a `theme/components/*.ts` file.

  (`.claude/registry/components.md:84`). **[V]**

  `origin/feature/f2r-implementation-workflow`, and **it contradicts `overrideStyling.md`** (which
  *is* on develop) on styling: it forbids `@chakra-ui/react` imports inside `ui-kits/` and mandates

  (`origin/feature/f2r-component-registry`, which has develop as an ancestor) carries

- **So the convention is real but only citable as code precedent, not as a rule.** Its authority is

## 1. The footer precedent, stated concretely

This is what "match the footer" actually means. All **[V]** via
`git show feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui:<path>`.

### 1.1 Layout

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/{index.tsx,index.stories.tsx}
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon/
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmLogo/
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmNavItem/
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmTextInput/
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmInputAction/
overrides/app/components/footer/{index.tsx,index.stories.tsx}       ← organism, top level, kebab-case (shadows base `footer`)
```

- Atoms and molecules live under `ui-kits/<tier>/<camelCase>/`, named `Zimm*`.
- The organism sits at `components/<name>/`. `footer/` is kebab-case because it **shadows** base
  SFCC `app/components/footer`. Zimmermann-authored components are camelCase
  (`.claude/rules/conventions.md` > File naming). **[V]**
- **No `organisms/` directory exists on either branch.** The footer organism is not in `ui-kits/`.
  **[I]** The working rule is: atoms + molecules are ui-kit inventory; organisms are page furniture
  and live where their SFCC counterpart would.

### 1.2 Composition — verified tier boundaries

| Component | Renders | Tier by the stated rule |
|---|---|---|
| `ZimmIcon` | `iconSizes` + an SVG map, no project component | atom **[V]** `zimmIcon/index.tsx:2,95` |
| `ZimmLogo` | inline SVG only | atom **[V]** |
| `ZimmNavItem` | `chakra.a` / `chakra.button` only | atom **[V]** `zimmNavItem/index.tsx:37,51` |
| `ZimmButton` | `ZimmIcon` | **[V]** `zimmButton/index.tsx:3` — an atom that renders an atom |
| `ZimmTextInput` | Chakra primitives, takes `trailing` as a slot | atom **[V]** |
| `ZimmInputAction` | `ZimmTextInput` + `ZimmButton` | molecule **[V]** `zimmInputAction/index.tsx:3-4` |
| `Footer` | `ZimmLogo`, `ZimmIcon`, `ZimmNavItem`, `ZimmButton`, `ZimmTextInput`, `ZimmInputAction` | organism **[V]** `footer/index.tsx:4-9` |

`ZimmButton` renders `ZimmIcon` and is still filed as an atom. **[I]** The team's operative rule is
looser than the one in the brief — an icon *rendered internally* still counts as an atom. Under the
brief's stricter rule `ZimmButton` would be a molecule. **Worth the Lead settling explicitly**, because
it changes where `zimmProductMeta` and the crumb link land. Everything below uses the brief's strict
rule and flags where the two disagree.

### 1.3 Styling — one recipe per component that has state, consumed via `__css`

- Recipes live in `overrides/app/theme/components/<camelCase>.ts` and are registered in
  `theme/components/index.ts`. Footer branch registers `Button, ZimmFooter, Header, ListMenu,
  ZimmNavItem, ZimmTextInput`. **[V]** `git show feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui:overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`
- Multipart recipes declare `parts: [...]` and the component reads
  `useMultiStyleConfig('ZimmFooter', {})` then applies `__css={styles.<part>}`. **Nothing is styled
  at the call site.** `footer.ts:40-46` states this as the file's contract. **[V]**
- Single-part atoms use `defineStyleConfig` + `useStyleConfig('ZimmNavItem', {variant})`. **[V]**
  `zimmNavItem.ts:74-78`, `zimmNavItem/index.tsx:33`
- **Not every atom gets a recipe.** `zimmIcon` and `zimmLogo` have none — they are pure geometry with
  no variant/state surface. `zimmButton` has none of its own; it consumes the base `Button` recipe.
  **[V]** The operative rule is: **a recipe when there is variant/size/state to express**, matching
  `overrideStyling.md` level 3.
- The organism recipe owns **all responsive layout for every part** — `footer.ts:40-46` says so
  explicitly, and `ZimmFooter.parts` runs to 20+ named parts. **[V]**

### 1.4 The `Zimm` prefix — the actual reason, verified

`overrides/app/theme/index.ts:64` composes with `extendTheme(baseTheme, overrides)`, which
**deep-merges**. A recipe key that collides with a base SFCC recipe key does not replace it — it
inherits it. **[V]**

Base SFCC registers these recipe keys (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/theme/index.js:38-52,89-103`): **[V]**

> `Breadcrumb`, `Header`, `Footer`, `CheckoutFooter`, `ListMenu`, `SwatchGroup`, `ImageGallery`,
> `Button`, plus `product-tile`, `drawer-menu`, `pagination`, `nested-accordion`, `locale-selector`…

The footer branch encodes the failure mode as a regression test —
`theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts:19-26`: **[V]**

> "A recipe key that collides with a base SFCC recipe. `theme/index.ts` composes with
> `extendTheme(baseTheme, overrides)`, which DEEP MERGES — a recipe named `Footer` does not replace
> SFCC's `Footer`, it inherits it. Shared part names then pick up base properties, and a key you add
> that the base lacks is appended last, so a CSS shorthand can silently reset a longhand the base
> declared earlier."

So: **`ZimmFooter`, not `Footer`.** And the un-prefixed `Button`, `Header`, `ListMenu` on both
branches are **deliberate** — those three *intend* to extend the base recipe. **[I]** but strongly
implied by them sitting alongside the prefixed pair in the same registration object.

**Direct consequence for SFCC-89:** any breadcrumb recipe **must** be `ZimmBreadcrumb`. Base
`theme/components/project/breadcrumb.js` declares `parts: ['container','icon','link']` with
`fontSize: 'sm'`, `icon.boxSize: 4`, `icon.color: 'grey'`, `link.paddingTop/Bottom: 3` — a naked
`Breadcrumb` key inherits every one of those. **[V]**

### 1.5 What gets a story, what gets a test

- **Every** component under `ui-kits/` and every organism has an `index.stories.tsx`. 12 story files
  on the footer branch, zero missing. **[V]**
- **No component has an `index.test.*`.** Vitest on the footer branch covers *theme recipes*
  (`recipeGuards.test.ts`, `zimmTextInput.test.ts`, `theme/index.test.tsx`, `fontFace.test.tsx`),
  *hooks* (`useSubscribeModal`, `useZimmTextInputState`, `useContentfulClient`, `useCountryConfig`)
  and *utils* (`safeHref`). **[V]**
- **The house pattern is: components → stories; recipes, hooks, utils → Vitest.** Component
  interaction goes in a story `play`, per `.claude/rules/testing.md`.
- Story titles use the `components.md` category tree with **no `Zimm` prefix in the title**:
  `Elements/ZimmButton`… wait — they *do* keep it (`Elements/ZimmNavItem`, `Forms/ZimmInputAction`),
  while this branch uses `Layout/PageToolbar` for `ZimmPageToolbar`. **[V]** Minor inconsistency;
  pick one. The footer branch is the larger sample.

### 1.6 How base/OOTB components are consumed

- `footer/index.tsx` imports base modules it is **not** overriding by their published path:
  `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/utils`, `.../hooks/use-multi-site`, `.../constants`. **[V]**
- Zimmermann-authored siblings are imported by **path alias** (`app/components/ui-kits/atoms/...`,
  `app/utils/safeHref`, `app/hooks/useSubscribeModal`) — **not** by the base path. **[V]** This is
  exactly what `overrideStyling.md` > "Importing an already-overridden component from a new
  component" requires, and the reason is Storybook/Vitest: `.storybook/main.js` aliases
  `@salesforce/retail-react-app` straight to `node_modules` and `vitest.config.ts` never loads the
  `ccExtensibility` resolver, so a base-path import of an overridden component silently renders the
  **unstyled base version** in stories and tests.
- `package.json` `ccExtensibility`: `{extends: "@salesforce/retail-react-app", overridesDir: "overrides"}`. **[V]**

## 6. What is custom vs out-of-the-box?

**Custom (Zimmermann-only, no SFCC ancestor)** — and Jira agrees: SFCC-89 carries the label `Custom`.

- All five text atoms. Base SFCC's PDP renders name/price inside `ProductView`; there is no
  component for a style code or model-fit line anywhere in the base app.
- `zimmBreadcrumb` — *functionally* a breadcrumb, but the Zimmermann design is a different component:
  literal `/` separator instead of `ChevronRightIcon`, a non-link terminal crumb carrying the product
  name, uppercase caption type, and placement **beneath** the gallery rather than above the content.
  Base SFCC's breadcrumb has no terminal-crumb concept at all. **[V]** base `breadcrumb/index.jsx:32-55`
- `ZimmPageToolbar` — a port of the handover `zimm-page-toolbar` element. No SFCC equivalent.
- `PdpProductInfo` — no SFCC equivalent.

**Out-of-the-box, staying that way:** `Skeleton`/`Box`/`Text` primitives, `useProduct`/`useCategory`,
`react-intl` currency formatting, and all six shared product components in §2.2.

**The grey area — say it out loud:** the *page* is an override of a base page, but ~everything inside
it is custom. The base `product-detail` page composes `ProductView` + `InformationAccordion` +
`RecommendedProducts` + `Island` + `Helmet`; ours composes two Zimmermann components. **[I]** That is
the right call for a luxury-brand rebuild, but it means "we override the PDP" understates it — we are
replacing the PDP and keeping the data layer. Worth being explicit with QA, because base-PDP
behaviours they may assume (404 on bad ID, SEO tags, deferred hydration) are simply gone.

## 7. What PR #57 got structurally wrong vs the footer precedent

All six are concrete and citable. None is a matter of taste.

### 7.1 Two of three new components have no theme recipe — and the one that has one over-escapes

- `breadcrumb/index.tsx:22-35` hardcodes `BASE_STYLE` and `LINK_PROPS` object literals in the
  component. Footer precedent: `zimmNavItem.ts` for exactly this component shape. **[V]**
- `zimmPageToolbar/index.tsx:28-33` hardcodes a per-variant `PADDING` map. This is *variant-keyed
  styling* — the textbook `overrideStyling.md` level-3 case. **[V]**
- Meanwhile `theme/components/pdpProductInfo.ts:23-33` invents `BODY_TEXT` / `PRICE_TEXT` /
  `META_TEXT` out of `var(--zimm-font-*)` escapes, with a comment claiming *"no entry in
  theme/foundation/typography.ts matches this family/weight/lineHeight combination."* **That comment
  is wrong.** **[V]**

  | Hand-rolled | Resolves to | Registered token | Identical? |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `PRICE_TEXT` (`pdpProductInfo.ts:30`) | body family / medium / 18px LH / 14px | `textStyles.price` = `FONT_MEDIUM, fontSizes['2xs']` (14px), `medium`, `lineHeights['2xs']` (18px), `letterSpacings.sm` (0) — `typography.ts:202-208` | **yes** |
  | `META_TEXT` (`pdpProductInfo.ts:33`) | body family / medium / 18px LH / 12px | `textStyles.caption` = same shape at `fontSizes['3xs']` (12px) — `typography.ts:143-149` | **yes** |

  And the Figma capture independently reaches the same conclusion: *"Price → `price` ✅ exact",
  "Model note → `caption` ✅ exact", "Style code → `caption` ✅ exact"* (req-figma.md §3). So three
  level-4 escape hatches can be deleted in favour of `textStyle: 'price'` / `textStyle: 'caption'`,
  and the file's stated blocker (*"the weight is still unresolved (FONT_REGULAR vs FONT_MEDIUM)
  pending UI-designer sign-off"*) is already answered by the approved design.

### 7.2 Only one of the new components is under `ui-kits/`

`ui-kits/` on this branch is `atoms/.gitkeep` + `atoms/zimmPageToolbar/`. **One component. No
`molecules/`, no `organisms/` directory.** **[V]** `pdpProductInfo/` sits at the top level of
`components/` alongside genuine kebab-case SFCC overrides, which makes a Zimmermann-authored
component look like an override at a glance. SFCC-91's `pdpColourSwatches` on
`origin/feature/SFCC-91_*` repeats the same mistake — so this is drifting into a second branch
already. **[V]**

### 7.3 The breadcrumb shadows a shared SFCC component the PLP consumes — the highest-risk item

**Verified base consumers of `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/breadcrumb`:** **[V]**
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/product-list/partials/page-header.jsx:14` → **the PLP**
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-view/index.jsx:45,75`

Because `ccExtensibility.overridesDir` is `overrides`, `overrides/app/components/breadcrumb/index.tsx`
**intercepts both of those imports in the real build.** What the PLP would receive:

| Base contract | Override | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `({categories, ...rest})`, `categories` optional | `categories` **required**, no `...rest` passthrough | PLP passes `category.parentCategoryTree`, which can be `undefined` → render throw |
| `categoryUrlBuilder(category, intl.locale)` | `encodeURI('/category/' + id)` | **locale prefix lost** on every PLP crumb across 11 locales / 8 storefronts |
| `<ChevronRightIcon>` separator | literal `/` text | **PLP breadcrumb visual silently changes**, unreviewed by design |
| `className="sf-breadcrumb"`, `data-testid="sf-crumb-item"` | neither | any selector on those breaks |
| `useStyleConfig('Breadcrumb')` | hardcoded objects | abandons the branch's own recipe pattern |
| Chakra `Breadcrumb`/`BreadcrumbItem`/`BreadcrumbLink` | raw `Box`/`Text` | loses Chakra's breadcrumb a11y primitives |

`overrideStyling.md` > "The SFCC bridge pattern (shared components only)" is explicit that a shared
internal dependency's **default export must stay a faithful, undecorated port**, with Zimmermann
styling behind a **named export**. This override exports the Zimmermann version as *both* named and
default (`breadcrumb/index.tsx:85-86`). **[V]**

**And it is invisible in CI.** Storybook aliases `@salesforce/retail-react-app` to `node_modules`
and Vitest never loads the resolver, so a PLP story or unit test would exercise the *base*
breadcrumb and pass while the shipped app renders ours. There is no test that can catch this today.

**Fix:** move to `ui-kits/molecules/zimmBreadcrumb/`, import it relatively from the PDP page, and
leave base `breadcrumb` untouched for SFCC-578 (Squad B) to decide. This also defuses the
ownership collision in req-jira.md §6.1.

Secondary, already flagged by CodeRabbit and still open: `breadcrumb/index.tsx:3` imports
`Box, Text` from `@chakra-ui/react` while `zimmPageToolbar/index.tsx:3` and
`product-detail/index.tsx:5` use the `shared/ui` barrel. **[V]** Pick one. (Note: overriding
`shared/ui/<Name>` intercepts nothing — the barrel has 103 relative re-exports, 212 base files
import the barrel, and **0** import a deep path. **[V]** verified by grep.)

`PdpProductInfo` renders five text elements and zero project components. SFCC-91 needs a product

(`/<li>\s*(Model is[^<]*?)\s*<\/li>/i`) across an 11-locale storefront. SFCC-26 created **`modelFit`**
specifically so this wouldn't be necessary, and the Jira comment history shows it was a deliberate
business decision to move away from the Magento behaviour this code reproduces. Either `c_modelFit`
isn't provisioned yet (→ interim workaround, must be labelled and ticketed for removal) or SFCC-26 is
stale. **Must be answered before sign-off.** req-jira.md §6.3.
